newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Slovnaft hopes to near 96 profit target.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Slovnaft hopes to near 96 profit target.

text.p: Slovakia's sole crude oil refiner, Slovnaft a.s., on Friday said it hopes to near its annual 1996 gross profit target of 2.4 billion crowns, despite higher costs due to a rise in world crude oil prices.
"We had planned lower profits in 1996 compared with 1995, and we hope to near the plan despite the crude oil price problems," Lubomir Zitnan, a Slovnaft spokesman, told Reuters.
"They were the main problem, and last year's costs are unusually high year-on-year," he said declining to provide specific profit or cost figures before releasing audited results in March.

Slovnaft had forecast 2.4 billion crowns in gross profit in 1996, after consolidated pre-tax profit of 3.4 billion crowns in 1995. Revenues totalled 39.6 billion crowns in 1996 after 35.818 billion in the previous year, Zitnan said.

The world crude oil price increase had prompted Slovnaft to iniciate several hikes in maximum prices of motor fuels, which are still state-controlled in Slovakia, totalling roughly 15-17 percent from 1996 beginning to end.
"But the year was favourable for purchase orders, which were overwhelming, boosting our exports to 17.6 billion crowns in 1996, from 15.6 billion the previous year," Zitnan added.
Slovnaft processed 5.2 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996, up slightly from 5.1 million in the previous year, Zitnan said.
From early March to end April, Slovnaft shut 70 percent of its refining capacity due to the maintanence project.
"We have made a great progress in preparation for broad investment projects, and we have fully secured their financing, which will total 11 billion crowns this year," Zitnan added.
